text_summary.body: Artaxerxes' letter authorises Ezra, priest and scribe, to go up with any Israelites who wish, to carry silver and gold for the Temple, to draw on the provincial treasury, and to appoint magistrates and judges who know the law of God.

setting.body: Artaxerxes I acceded in late 465/early 464 (Elephantine papyrus Cowley 6); his seventh Babylonian year began 8 Apr 458 and its fifth month (Ab) on 4 Aug 458. Driver notes that the decree says nothing about rebuilding Jerusalem.

constraints.subject: evt_01M4V10B5RYFVXPCH4BAVN77BK
constraints.textual_assertion: went up to Jerusalem in the seventh year of Artaxerxes the king
assumptions: Artaxerxes of Ezra 7 = Artaxerxes I (the majority view among sources read; Newton reports Funccius placing Ezra under Artaxerxes II).
Nisan reckoning: year 7 began 1 Nisan = 8 Apr 458; Ezra arrived 1 Ab = 4 Aug 458 (Parker & Dubberstein table).

terminology.gloss: Here an expert in the Law of Moses, not merely a copyist (Guzik, Kidner).

competing_reconstructions.label: 458 BC (Nisan reckoning)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Departure 1 Nisan = 8 Apr 458; arrival 1 Ab = 4 Aug 458.

competing_reconstructions.label: 457 BC
proponents: I. Newton (Julian Period 4257 for the journey; autumn reckoning)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Counts the decree's execution from the following autumn or uses a different year count.

competing_reconstructions.label: Ezra under Artaxerxes II
competing_reconstructions.summary: Would move the decree to 398 BC; not researched further here.

competing_reconstructions.label: Ezra under Xerxes (seventh year)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Josephus names Xerxes as Ezra's king and the high priest Joacim son of Jeshua.

competing_reconstructions.label: Ezra after Nehemiah, early fourth century
proponents: W. H. Kosters: 398 B.C. (as reported by Batten)
competing_reconstructions.summary: Only the Chronicler names the king; Ezra himself says "the king"; the Aramaic letter is not authentic in its present form.

open_questions: The Ezra–Nehemiah order (Artaxerxes I or II for Ezra) not researched from modern studies.

not_applicable.commentary: Enduring Word on Ezra/Nehemiah was not consulted in this Daniel session; Guzik's dates are recorded on the seventy-weeks prophecy.
